summary: Audited /Users/atharv/buisnessfind/server.js (520 lines), data/store.js (293), .env.example and package.json line by line. The app cannot boot: server.js:9 requires './seo-content' which does not exist. Verified path handling, dispatch ordering, quota accounting and store durability empirically with node. KEY ANSWERS TO THE NINE QUESTIONS: (1) BOOT BLOCKER. Only two use sites exist. server.js:440 `seoPages[slug]` and server.js:465 `Object.keys(seoPages)`. `categoryList` is imported at line 9 and NEVER used anywhere (grep-confirmed) — the module must still export it or destructuring yields undefined harmlessly, but it is dead weight. Required export shape: module.exports = { seoPages, categoryList } seoPages: a plain object keyed by URL slug WITHOUT a leading slash (sitemapXml emits `/${key}`, handleSeoPage receives `pathname.slice(1)`). Slugs must be URL-safe and must NOT collide with any real static asset name or any /api/ path. Each page object needs exactly these keys, all consumed by handleSeoPage at lines 443-458: title (string) -> AND og:title AND jsonLd.name description (string) -> meta description AND og:description AND jsonLd.description h1 (string) -> <h1> lede (string) -> <p class="lede"> category (string) -> data-category on #app-embed; MUST be one of the 12 keys of CATEGORY_TYPES (server.js:43-56: restaurants, cafes, groceries, malls, clothing, pharmacies, gyms, salons, atms, petrol, bakeries, bars) or the frontend cannot map it to a Places includedType body (string, RAW HTML, injected unescaped into <section class="seo-copy">) faq (OPTIONAL array of { q: string, a: string }; both injected as raw HTML). If present it MUST be an array — `page.faq.map` at line 457 throws on a truthy non-array. Anything nested (e.g. an `items` array) is ignored — nothing else is read. jsonLd is built entirely by the server from title/description, so pages supply no schema. (2) DISPATCH ORDERING. server.js:480 runs handleSeoPage on EVERY path with length > 1, before both the /api/ branch (482) and serveStatic. It does NOT shadow /styles.css or /app.js today, because handleSeoPage returns false when the slug is not a key — so the frontend CAN be served. But it is a live hazard on two counts: (a) any future slug equal to an asset name silently shadows that asset; (b) `seoPages[slug]` is an unguarded lookup, so GET /constructor, /toString, /valueOf, /__proto__, /hasOwnProperty all return a 200 HTML page full of the literal string "undefined" instead of a 404 or the SPA (verified: `Boolean({}['constructor'])` is true). (3) EMPTY public/. Yes, it breaks everything. GET / maps to /index.html, which HAS an extension, so the SPA-fallback branch at line 404 is skipped entirely, readFile fails and the site returns `<h1>Not found</h1>` with status 404. Extensionless routes (/friends) fall back to public/index.html which also does not exist -> 404. The SEO pages reference /styles.css and /app.js which would also 404. serveStatic itself is not broken — it just has nothing to serve. (4) COST CAPS. tryConsume fires BEFORE the Google call in all three helpers (158, 192, 226), and store.tryConsume is fully synchronous read-check-increment with no await inside, so a concurrent burst inside one process CANNOT overshoot the cap. Two real problems instead: a FAILED Google call (502, DNS error, timeout) still consumes budget with no refund; and worse, budget is consumed BEFORE input validation — placesNearby consumes then rejects an unknown category at line 161-162, so an unauthenticated attacker exhausts the 500/day nearby cap with 500 requests that never touch Google. /api/nearby and /api/place are unauthenticated and only IP-rate-limited at 30/min, so a handful of IPs drain the whole daily budget in minutes and the app is dead for real users until UTC midnight. Also `save()` after increment is never awaited, so a crash loses increments (undercount, cap overshoot across restarts), and multiple processes sharing store.json would double-count. (5) UNGUARDED LOOKUPS. `routes` is correctly guarded with Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call (line 497); `seoPages[slug]` (440) and `MIME[ext]` (408) are not — seoPages is exploitable as described in (2). serveStatic's `filePath.startsWith(PUBLIC_DIR)` is missing the trailing separator, but I verified it is NOT exploitable over HTTP: WHATWG URL normalizes ../, //../ and %2e%2e/ out of pathname before it reaches path.resolve, and the resolve base is always PUBLIC_DIR + './...'. It stays a latent footgun (a sibling dir `public-old` would pass the check) and should be fixed anyway. Separate real bug: pathname is never percent-decoded, so /foo%20bar.css looks for a file literally named `foo%20bar.css`. (6) XSS in pageShell. The content is author-controlled (seo-content.js), not user input, and the only URL-derived value (`canonical`, from slug) is reachable only when slug is a literal key — so there is no reflected XSS today. But title/description are interpolated into HTML ATTRIBUTES with no quote escaping (lines 423-427), so a single `"` or `<` in copy silently breaks the head; and body/faq are documented-raw HTML with zero sanitisation, which makes seo-content.js a full XSS surface the moment any of it is generated, templated, or CMS-sourced. (7) SECRET LEAK. Clean. /api/config (routes.config, 242-248) returns only { live, mapsBrowserKey, categories }; GOOGLE_PLACES_SERVER_KEY is only ever sent in the X-Goog-Api-Key header or the server-side geocode URL and never reaches the client. One adjacent leak: Google's raw error body is passed to the browser verbatim via `Places ${res.status}: ${body.slice(0,300)}` (180, 205). (8) STORE INTEGRITY. The write queue serialises correctly and snapshots JSON at call time, so ordering is safe. But writeFile is non-atomic (truncate-then-write), and load() responds to ANY parse failure by silently resetting to emptyDb() — a crash mid-write therefore wipes every user, session, friendship and saved place with a one-line console message, and the next save() overwrites the corrupt file permanently. removeFriend deletes both share keys but leaves db.locations[friendId] on disk forever, and leaves the accepted friendRequest row behind. Also `{...emptyDb(), ...JSON.parse(raw)}` is a shallow merge, so a store.json containing `"users": null` makes db.users null and every request TypeErrors. (9) CRASH PATHS. No timeout or AbortSignal on any of the three outbound fetches — a hung Google socket hangs the client request indefinitely and holds a connection. No process-level unhandledRejection/uncaughtException handlers, and the dispatcher's catch calls sendJson with no res.headersSent guard, so a post-send throw becomes ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT inside the catch of an unawaited async handler and kills the process on Node >=15. crypto.scryptSync (N=16384) blocks the event loop on every login and signup, and /api/auth/* has no IP rate limit at all — unauthenticated POST /api/auth/signup is both an event-loop DoS and an unbounded account-creation/disk-growth vector. SPEC GAPS (locked decisions not implemented): live location is persisted to store.json and never expires, the exact inverse of "live coordinates stay in memory, never on disk" and the 15min/1hr/8hr time-boxing; there is no check-in primitive anywhere despite check-ins being the default social primitive; there is no emailVerified field or gate on the friends surface.

issues.issue: Line 9 `require('./seo-content')` refers to a file that does not exist. The process throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND at load; `npm start` never binds a port. Nothing in the app works.
issues.fix: Create /Users/atharv/buisnessfind/seo-content.js exporting `{ seoPages, categoryList }`. seoPages is a plain object keyed by leading-slash-free URL slug (sitemapXml emits `/${key}`; handleSeoPage receives pathname.slice(1)). Every value object needs: title (string, used in <title>, og:title, jsonLd.name), description (string, meta description + og:description + jsonLd.description), h1 (string), lede (string), category (string, MUST be one of the 12 CATEGORY_TYPES keys at server.js:43-56), body (RAW HTML string, injected unescaped), and optional faq (array of {q,a}, both raw HTML — if present it must be a real array or line 457's .map throws). No other key is read. categoryList is imported but never used (grep-confirmed): either drop it from the destructure at line 9 or export it as the array of {slug, label, category} that the frontend nav will consume. Slugs must not collide with any file in public/ or with any /api/ path.

issues.issue: save() at line 45-51 does a non-atomic fsp.writeFile (truncate then write) while load() at 33-41 silently falls back to emptyDb() on any parse error. A crash, full disk, or SIGKILL mid-write leaves truncated JSON; the next boot wipes every user, session, friendship, share and saved place with only a console.error, then the first save() overwrites the corrupt file so the data is unrecoverable.
issues.fix: Write atomically: `await fsp.writeFile(FILE + '.tmp', snapshot, {mode:0o600}); await fsp.rename(FILE + '.tmp', FILE);` (rename is atomic on the same filesystem). In load(), distinguish ENOENT (first run, emptyDb is correct) from a parse/read failure — on parse failure rename the bad file to store.json.corrupt-<timestamp> and throw so the server refuses to start rather than silently starting empty.

issues.issue: placesNearby consumes daily budget at line 158 BEFORE validating the category at line 161, and placeDetails consumes at 192 before any validation of placeId. Unauthenticated GET /api/nearby?lat=1&lng=1&category=bogus returns 400 having burned a nearby unit without ever calling Google. With the 30/min IP limit, ~17 minutes from one IP (or seconds from a few) drains NEARBY_DAILY_CAP=500 and the whole app returns 429 to real users until UTC midnight.
issues.fix: Move every validation above the tryConsume call in all three helpers: resolve includedType and reject unknown categories, range-check lat (-90..90) and lng (-180..180), clamp radius to a positive value (Math.min(Math.max(Number(radius)||1500, 1), 50000) — currently a negative radius reaches Google), and sanity-check placeId shape, all before store.tryConsume.

issues.issue: A failed Google call still consumes budget. Lines 180 and 205 throw on !res.ok, and a network/DNS failure throws from fetch itself, after tryConsume has already incremented the counter. A Google outage or a bad/revoked API key burns the entire 500/200/200 daily budget in failed 502s while serving zero results.
issues.fix: Add a store.refund(kind) that decrements db.apiUsage[kind] (floored at 0) and call it in the !res.ok and catch paths of placesNearby/placeDetails/geocode — at minimum for 5xx, network errors and 401/403 (auth misconfiguration), which are not the caller's fault. Keep charging for 4xx caused by caller input.

issues.issue: No timeout or AbortSignal on any outbound fetch (lines 164, 195, 232). A hung TCP connection to Google leaves the client request open indefinitely, pins a socket and a Node handle, and under load exhausts the connection pool — the server appears frozen with no error logged.
issues.fix: Pass `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(8000)` to all three fetch calls and catch the AbortError, mapping it to a 504 with a friendly message. Also set an explicit server.requestTimeout / server.headersTimeout.

issues.issue: /api/auth/* is completely exempt from tooManyRequests (the rate-limit calls at 486 and 493 cover only /api/friends and nearby/place/geocode). Both signup and login run crypto.scryptSync with N=16384, which blocks the single-threaded event loop for tens of milliseconds each. Unauthenticated POST /api/auth/signup in a loop both freezes the whole server for every other user and creates unlimited accounts, each triggering a full rewrite of store.json.
issues.fix: Apply tooManyRequests(ip, 10, 60_000) to every /api/auth/* path before handleAuth, and add a stricter per-IP signup cap (e.g. 3/hour). Switch hashPassword/verifyPassword to the async crypto.scrypt (promisified) so hashing runs on the threadpool instead of the event loop.

issues.issue: Unguarded lookup `seoPages[slug]` at line 440 hits Object.prototype. GET /constructor, /toString, /valueOf, /hasOwnProperty and /__proto__ all produce a truthy `page`, so handleSeoPage returns true and emits a 200 HTML document whose title, description, h1, lede, body and data-category are all the literal string 'undefined' — shadowing both the 404 and the SPA fallback, and feeding garbage pages to crawlers.
issues.fix: Guard the lookup: `const page = Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(seoPages, slug) ? seoPages[slug] : null; if (!page || typeof page !== 'object') return false;` Additionally pre-filter with a strict slug regex (/^[a-z0-9-]+$/) before the lookup.

issues.issue: Dispatch ordering: handleSeoPage runs at line 480 on every non-root path, before the /api/ branch at 482 and before serveStatic. It does not shadow assets today only because no slug happens to equal an asset name — but a slug named 'app.js', 'styles.css' or 'manifest.json' would silently serve an SEO page in place of the real file, and a slug beginning 'api/' would shadow an endpoint, with no error anywhere.
issues.fix: Move the API branch above the SEO branch, and gate SEO on a slug that cannot be an asset: skip handleSeoPage when path.extname(pathname) is non-empty or pathname starts with '/api/'. Add a boot-time assertion that no key of seoPages matches a filename in public/ or starts with 'api'.

issues.issue: updateLocation (222-225) writes friend coordinates into db.locations and persists them to store.json, and friendLocations (227-237) returns them with no age check. This directly violates the locked decision that live coordinates stay in memory and never on disk, and there is no 15min/1hr/8hr expiry — a location shared once is readable by that friend forever, surviving restarts, and sits in a plaintext JSON file.
issues.fix: Move locations out of db entirely into a module-level `const liveLocations = new Map()` that is never serialised (remove `locations` from emptyDb and from the save snapshot). Store { lat, lng, updatedAt, expiresAt } and have updateLocation take a duration from the allowed set (15m/1h/8h) and compute expiresAt. friendLocations must drop any entry where expiresAt <= Date.now(); add an unref'd sweep interval. Add the separate check-in primitive (a persisted { userId, placeId, name, createdAt }) that the spec makes the default.

issues.issue: No email-verification gate on the friends surface. handleFriends (329-367) only calls requireUser; store.js has no emailVerified/verificationToken field at all. Anyone who signs up with an address they do not own can immediately send friend requests and receive shared locations, defeating the stated rule that verification gates the friends surface.
issues.fix: Add `emailVerified: false` plus a hashed verification token and expiry to createUser, expose /api/auth/verify, and add `if (!user.emailVerified) throw Object.assign(new Error('Verify your email first.'), {status: 403})` at the top of handleFriends and handleLocation. publicUser should surface emailVerified so the UI can prompt.

issues.issue: MIME table (line 398) covers only .html/.js/.css/.svg/.json. Every .png, .jpg, .webp, .ico, .woff2 and .webmanifest is served as application/octet-stream, and `MIME[ext]` is itself an unguarded prototype lookup. Browsers refuse to render map marker images and refuse to load fonts, and the favicon and web manifest are ignored — silently, with a 200 status.
issues.fix: Add png, jpg/jpeg, webp, avif, ico, woff2, webmanifest, txt and xml entries, and read it with Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(MIME, ext) or convert MIME to `Object.create(null)`/a Map. Send cache headers too: immutable long max-age for hashed assets, no-cache for index.html.

issues.issue: geocode (225-237) never checks res.ok or the Google `status` field. A REQUEST_DENIED (bad key), OVER_QUERY_LIMIT or an HTML error page returns HTTP 200 with no results, so the user is told 'Could not find that location.' — masking a configuration outage as a user typo. If results exist but geometry is absent, `first.geometry.location.lat` throws a TypeError and returns 500.
issues.fix: After the fetch: check res.ok, then branch on json.status — 'OK'/'ZERO_RESULTS' handled normally, everything else thrown as a 502 with a logged (not user-facing) detail. Guard `first?.geometry?.location?.lat` and reject non-finite values. Also cap query length (e.g. 200 chars) before consuming budget.

issues.issue: Google's raw error body is relayed to the browser at lines 180 and 205 via `Places ${res.status}: ${body.slice(0,300)}` — the outer catch (501-505) sends err.message straight to the client. This exposes internal request details, quota/project state and Google's diagnostic text to unauthenticated callers of /api/nearby and /api/place.
issues.fix: Log the full body server-side with console.error and throw a generic user-facing message ('Search is temporarily unavailable.') with status 502. More broadly, in the catch at 501, only send err.message when status < 500; for 5xx send a fixed string.

issues.issue: pageShell (417-437) interpolates title and description into HTML attribute values (`content="${description}"`, `<title>${title}`) with no escaping, and injects page.body and page.faq entries as raw HTML. A single double-quote or < in copy breaks the head and can terminate the attribute; the moment any of that copy becomes templated or user/CMS-sourced it is a stored XSS.
issues.fix: Add `const esc = s => String(s).replace(/&/g,'&').replace(/</g,'<').replace(/>/g,'>').replace(/"/g,'"')` and wrap title, description, canonical, h1, lede, page.category and every f.q/f.a. Keep page.body raw only if it stays a hand-authored constant, and document that; the JSON.stringify'd jsonLd also needs `</` escaped to `<\/` to prevent script-tag breakout.

issues.issue: removeFriend (186-192) deletes both share keys but leaves db.locations[friendId] and the accepted friendRequest row on disk indefinitely. The ex-friend's last known coordinates persist in store.json forever even though nobody can read them, and friendRequests grows without bound.
issues.fix: On removeFriend, also drop any friendRequest rows between the pair, and delete the location entry if that user has no remaining sharers. Once locations move to the in-memory Map, drop the map entry too. Add an equivalent cleanup for savedPlaces and sessions if a user is ever deleted.

issues.issue: load() at line 36 does a shallow merge `{...emptyDb(), ...JSON.parse(raw)}` with no schema validation. A store.json containing `"users": null` (or an object where an array is expected) makes db.users null, and every subsequent request throws TypeError on .find — a permanent 500 on all routes with no useful diagnostic. `apiUsage: null` likewise makes resetUsageIfNewDay throw on db.apiUsage.date, taking down all Google endpoints.
issues.fix: After the merge, coerce each field to its expected type: arrays via `Array.isArray(x) ? x : []` for users/friendRequests/friendships/savedPlaces, plain-object checks for sessions/shares/locations, and rebuild apiUsage from scratch if it is not an object with a string date and numeric counters.

issues.issue: Setting a cap to 0 to disable an endpoint does not work. Lines 35-37 use `Number(process.env.NEARBY_DAILY_CAP) || 500`, and 0 is falsy, so PLACE_DETAILS_DAILY_CAP=0 silently becomes 200 — the operator believes the expensive reviews endpoint is off while it is billing at full rate.
issues.fix: Use an explicit parse: `const num = (v, d) => { const n = Number(v); return Number.isFinite(n) && n >= 0 ? n : d; }` and apply it to PORT and all three caps. Note in .env.example that 0 disables an endpoint.

issues.issue: Account enumeration on two surfaces. POST /api/auth/signup returns a distinct 409 'An account with that email already exists.' (line 303), and POST /api/friends/request returns 404 'No account with that email.' (346). Since signup is unauthenticated and unthrottled, anyone can test arbitrary addresses for membership. Login also returns 401 without running scrypt when the user is unknown (315), a timing oracle.
issues.fix: Make signup respond identically whether or not the email exists (202 'Check your email to finish signing up' — the verification mail then differentiates), and make /api/friends/request return the same 201-style acknowledgement for unknown addresses without revealing existence. In login, run a dummy scrypt with a fixed salt when the user is not found so both branches take the same time.

issues.issue: The dispatcher's catch at 501-505 calls sendJson unconditionally with no res.headersSent check, and there are no process-level unhandledRejection/uncaughtException handlers. Any throw after a response has begun becomes ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT inside the catch of an async handler nobody awaits (http.createServer ignores the returned promise), which on Node >=15 terminates the process and drops every in-flight request.
issues.fix: In the catch: `if (res.headersSent) { res.destroy(); return; }` before sendJson, and wrap the sendJson itself in try/catch. Add `process.on('unhandledRejection', e => console.error('[unhandled]', e))` and an uncaughtException handler that logs and exits deliberately. Run under a supervisor that restarts.

issues.issue: pruneSessions() is called exactly once, at boot (server.js:514). A long-running server accumulates every session record for the full 30-day TTL and beyond — expired sessions are rejected at check time but never removed, so db.sessions and every store.json write grow monotonically with login churn.
issues.fix: Schedule it: `setInterval(pruneSessions, 6*60*60*1000).unref()` inside store.js, and also cap sessions per user (drop the oldest beyond, say, 10).

issues.issue: serveStatic (400-413) never percent-decodes the pathname before resolving it, so a request for /logo%20mark.svg looks for a file literally named 'logo%20mark.svg' and 404s. Any asset with a space or non-ASCII character in its name is unreachable.
issues.fix: Decode inside a try/catch (`let rel; try { rel = decodeURIComponent(pathname); } catch { return 400; }`), reject any decoded string containing '\0' or '..' segments, then resolve.

issues.issue: The containment check `filePath.startsWith(PUBLIC_DIR)` at line 403 omits the trailing separator. I verified it is not exploitable over HTTP today (WHATWG URL normalizes ../, //../ and %2e%2e/ out of pathname before path.resolve, and the resolve base is always PUBLIC_DIR + './...'), but it would accept a sibling directory such as /Users/atharv/buisnessfind/public-old, so it breaks silently under any refactor that changes how rel is built.
issues.fix: Compare against `PUBLIC_DIR + path.sep` (and allow the exact PUBLIC_DIR itself), or use `path.relative(PUBLIC_DIR, filePath)` and reject when it starts with '..' or is absolute.

issues.issue: Route handlers never await save(), so /api/auth/signup returns 201 and sets a session cookie before the user row is durable. A crash in that window leaves a browser holding a valid-looking cookie for a user that no longer exists — userForToken returns null via findById and the client sees itself silently logged out with no error.
issues.fix: Make the mutating store functions async and `await save()` before the handler responds, at least for createUser, createSession and savePlace. tryConsume can stay fire-and-forget.

issues.issue: A declined friend request creates no block. respondToRequest sets status 'declined', and pendingRequestBetween only matches status==='pending', so the sender can immediately re-send an unlimited number of requests — a harassment vector on a friends-only social product with no block list.
issues.fix: Add a blocks collection (or a cooldown honouring the most recent 'declined' row) and reject sendFriendRequest when a block exists or a decline is less than N days old. Expose a /api/friends/block endpoint.

issues.issue: Rate limiting keys on req.socket.remoteAddress (line 475). Behind any reverse proxy or CDN every visitor shares one IP, so the 30/min quota endpoint limit and the per-IP login throttle either lock out all users at once or, on a shared NAT, are trivially bypassed by a single attacker with several egress IPs. There is also no rate limit on /api/location, /api/saved or /api/config.
issues.fix: Add a TRUST_PROXY env flag; when set, take the left-most entry of X-Forwarded-For, otherwise keep remoteAddress. Apply a modest per-IP limit to /api/location and /api/saved as well, and cap savedPlaces per user in store.savePlace (which currently validates nothing about placeId/name/category and allows unbounded rows).

issues.issue: usageRemaining is exported by store.js and imported into scope but never called anywhere in server.js (grep-confirmed), so the client has no way to display remaining daily quota and users only discover the cap when a search fails with a 429.
issues.fix: Include remaining counts in routes.config: `quota: { nearby: store.usageRemaining('nearby', NEARBY_CAP), place: store.usageRemaining('place', PLACE_CAP), geocode: store.usageRemaining('geocode', GEOCODE_CAP) }` so the frontend can warn before the cap is hit.

issues.issue: routes.config returns `live: Boolean(SERVER_KEY)` but `mapsBrowserKey: LIVE ? BROWSER_KEY : null`. With a server key set and GOOGLE_MAPS_BROWSER_KEY blank, the client is told live:true and handed an empty-string key, so the map silently fails to initialise with no actionable message. The generic dispatcher also ignores req.method entirely, so POST /api/nearby is treated as GET and the body is never drained.
issues.fix: Compute LIVE as `Boolean(SERVER_KEY && BROWSER_KEY)` or return a separate `mapEnabled` flag, and warn at boot when only one key is present. Add a method check (GET-only) to the generic route dispatcher at 492-500.

issues.issue: `"name": "buisnessfind"` and the description carry the misspelling, as do the hard-coded canonical/sitemap/robots hosts (https://buisnessfind.app at server.js:442, 466, 478) and the seed email default admin@buisnessfind.app. The spelling is being corrected to businessfind at build time, so these all become wrong URLs baked into canonical tags and the sitemap — actively harmful for SEO.
issues.fix: Rename to businessfind in package.json, and replace the three hard-coded hosts with a SITE_ORIGIN env var (default http://localhost:${PORT}) used by pageShell's canonical, sitemapXml and robots.txt. Add SITE_ORIGIN to .env.example. Also add `"type": "commonjs"` explicitly, since the frontend is ES modules and the ambiguity will bite.
